hardware.navigation_buttons: GPIO14 short press Next, GPIO0 short press Back
hardware.approval_buttons: GPIO14 long press Approve, GPIO0 long press Reject

procedure: Built the T-Display S3 firmware with ESP-IDF v5.5.4 from /Users/vincenzo/esp/esp-idf-v5.5.4/export.sh.
Sent a valid serial sign_event request so the display entered a live trusted-review session.
Observed the first live request-derived review page on the display.
Pressed the vendor-documented KEY/GPIO14 button briefly to navigate forward.
Pressed the vendor-documented BOOT/GPIO0 button briefly to navigate backward.
Reworked the boot screen after the manual check so reboot shows Ready/No request instead of a fake event-review page, then rebuilt, reflashed, and reran protocol smoke.
expected_result: A live sign_event request shows Event Page 1/4, short KEY/GPIO14 moves to Content Page 2/4, short BOOT/GPIO0 returns to Event Page 1/4, touch is not used for consent, and the protocol still returns signing_disabled.
observed_result: Manual physical confirmation showed short KEY/GPIO14 advanced from Event Page 1/4 to Content Page 2/4 and short BOOT/GPIO0 returned to Event Page 1/4. After unplug/replug, the RAM-only active review session was lost as expected; firmware was then updated so reboot shows Ready/No request. The final flashed firmware passed 33 USB serial smoke exchanges and sign_event remained signing_disabled.
limitations: This is display and physical navigation validation only; it is not a production signing acceptance test.
Long-press approve/reject mapping is compiled but has not yet been treated as authorization for signing because sign_event remains signing_disabled.
The device stores the active review session only in RAM; power cycling clears it and requires a new request.
No persistent key custody, secure boot, flash encryption, debug-lock, enclosure, or production approval policy was validated.
